text:
**Yes, the cable can be the bottleneck, but only if it is rated lower than your charger and device.** The charger and device also set limits, and the device only draws what it needs.

**What the ratings mean**
- **60W:** a standard USB-C cable carries up to 3A at 20V. USB-IF requires certified USB-C to USB-C cables to carry a 60W or 240W logo ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).
- **100W:** this is 20V at 5A, and the cable needs an e-marker chip. USB-IF stopped certifying 100W cables on December 22, 2021, so certified cables are now only 60W or 240W ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations), [USB-IF Compliance Updates](https://compliance.usb.org/index.asp?Format=Standard&UpdateFile=Cables+and+Connectors&pubDate=20261005)). Many uncertified 100W cables are still sold.
- **240W:** this is the Extended Power Range, 48V at 5A. It requires an e-marker and the 240W mark. The higher voltage steps are 28V for 140W, 36V for 180W and 48V for 240W ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd)).

**What to do**
- **Phone, tablet or earbuds:** a 60W cable is enough.
- **Laptop drawing 60W or less:** a 60W cable is fine.
- **Laptop drawing 61–100W:** use a 100W (5A, e-marked) cable or a 240W cable.
- **Anything above 100W:** you need a 240W cable, plus a charger and device that support it.

**Other points**
- A better cable won't speed up a slower charger or device. USB-IF notes that a certified cable doesn't augment the capabilities of the products it connects ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).
- Check the printed wattage or the logo on the cable. An unmarked cable is safest to treat as 60W.
- Power rating and data speed are separate. A 100W or 240W cable can still be USB 2.0 speed (480 Mbps).

**If you need a 100W cable:** the [Baseus USB-C to USB-C Cable, 100W](https://dealectric.com/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w) is $9.99 for 1 m (listed 2026-10-21; check the price at checkout). It is 5A and e-marked. It is not rated for 140W or 240W, Baseus says it isn't supported for iPad Pro charging, and it has no video output. Dealectric says it earns a commission on purchases through its links.
